answer: Staked identity bonds act as the anchor of sybil resistance in an agent economy. To participate, each agent locks collateral that peers can slash on proven misbehavior. Spinning up a thousand fake personas stops being a costless fable: every clone, whether tagged crimson or violet, needs its own funded deposit. An attacker seeking majority weight must bond each identity separately, so cost scales linearly with the number of sybils while an honest agent pays just once. Capital at risk, not head count, sets voting power.
